title: Singing back
hook: in the gurdwara the sangat sings the refrain back to the singers

segments.voice: Yesterday, one line of gurbani, sung until it's yours. Your line was one line is enough.

In a stadium, one section starts a song, and it rolls around the stands until thousands of strangers are singing the same words. Nobody sounds good alone. Together, it's enormous. Or something smaller: a birthday table where everyone's slightly off key, and it's still the best part of the night. Something happens when voices join that doesn't happen to any voice alone. Now a gurdwara in the evening. The ragis at the front sing a line of a shabad. They pause. The whole room sings the line back. They sing the next. The room answers again.
screen: `A STADIUM OF STRANGERS SINGING.` → `THE BIRTHDAY TABLE, OFF KEY.` → `THE ROOM SINGS IT BACK.`

segments.voice: Sangat. You met the word on day fifteen: the congregation, the company you keep. Today you hear it. In many gurdwaras, especially at evening programs and in some styles of kirtan, the singers lead a line and the sangat sings it back. Call and answer. A child's voice next to a grandfather's, a beginner next to someone who's known the shabad for a lifetime, all on the same line. Nobody is performing. Everybody is part of it. Sikhs set great store by this. The Gurus taught that the company you keep shapes the person you become, and that the true sangat has a mark you can recognize. Guru Nanak asks in the Guru Granth Sahib, in paraphrase: how is the true congregation known? And he answers: it's where the one Name is spoken. Not a building. Not a membership. A gathering of people remembering God together. That's why singing back matters. Alone, you can drift, lose the tune, forget the words, get self-conscious. In the sangat, the voices around you carry you. When you falter, someone else has the line; when they falter, you do. And the singing does to the room what seva does in the kitchen: it dissolves the hierarchy for a while. This week you listened for instruments, found the rahao, read along, hummed, sang Waheguru, learned one line. All of it was practice for this: your voice, taking its place among the others. You don't have to sing well. You just have to sing with.
screen: `SANGAT — THE COMPANY YOU KEEP.` · `THE RAGIS LEAD, THE ROOM ANSWERS.` · `WHERE THE ONE NAME IS SPOKEN.` · `THE OTHERS CARRY YOU.` · then, large: `VOICES TOGETHER.`

segments.voice: If you can, play a recording of kirtan where the sangat sings back, as many gurdwara recordings and live streams have, and when the singers lead a line, sing it back with the room, even quietly. If you can't find one, sing along once with any song you know, all the way through, and notice how much easier it is when you're not alone.
Sangat. The congregation, singing back, voice with voice. Your week: instruments, rahao, reading along, humming, Waheguru, one line, and the sangat.
Your line: voices together. When you falter, someone else has the line. That's the week, and day one hundred twelve.
